title: Narrowband searches for continuous gravitational waves from known pulsars in the first two parts of the fourth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA observing run
extended_summary:
This paper is not an education study and does not address AI tools, K-12 science learning, or any instructional intervention. Instead, it reports astrophysical searches for narrowband continuous gravitational waves from known pulsars using data from the first two parts of the fourth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA observing run.

The work describes a physics data-analysis approach for detecting continuous gravitational-wave signals, focusing on known pulsars as sources. It is a large collaborative observational paper in gravitational-wave astronomy, not an educational experiment, and it does not include students, teachers, schools, or learning outcomes.

Accordingly, there is no population, user type, implementation context, or educational outcome to extract for the requested K-12 science evidence review. The paper’s conclusions concern gravitational-wave search results rather than causally comparing AI-powered tools with non-AI comparators in science education.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a physics/gravitational-wave astronomy article, not an education study, and it does not evaluate any AI-powered educational intervention or K-12 science learning outcome. It contains no relevant empirical methodology for the requested taxonomy.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational impact is reported because the paper is unrelated to K-12 science instruction, scientific reasoning, or inquiry outcomes. There is no intervention-comparator evidence to classify.
